summary: Claude Code, the coding agent that works on this repository, keeps per-session state in a .claude/ directory at the repository root. When an agent starts an isolated task, Claude Code creates a Git worktree, a second working copy of the repository, under .claude/worktrees/. Git sees that directory as new, untracked content, so git status lists .claude/ in every checkout an agent has touched.

This pull request adds one line, /.claude/, to .gitignore, so that Git ignores the whole directory at the repository root. Nothing under .claude/ is tracked on main, so the line hides no committed file. The repository's shared agent instructions live in AGENTS.md at the root, outside the ignored directory.

The description also says that the repository can later share one Claude Code setting, such as .claude/settings.json, by adding a !/.claude/settings.json line. The review found that this does not work with the pattern as written, as the note on the line explains.

groups.title: Git ignores the .claude directory
groups.kicker: One new ignore pattern for Claude Code's per-session state
intro: .gitignore lists the paths Git leaves out of git status and git add. It held one pattern, /target, for Cargo's build output. The new pattern /.claude/ matches only the .claude directory at the repository root, because of the leading slash, and only a directory, because of the trailing slash.

A pattern that names a directory makes Git skip the directory without reading it. That is why a later ! line, which re-includes a path, cannot bring back a file inside it. A pattern that names the directory's contents, /.claude/*, ignores the same files and still lets a ! line re-include one of them.

checks.text: Nothing under .claude/ is tracked on main: git ls-files .claude prints nothing, so the pattern hides no committed file.

A later !/.claude/settings.json line cannot re-include the file, because Git does not look inside a directory this pattern excludes. In a scratch repository with that negation below a directory pattern, git status stays silent about the new file and git add refuses it as ignored. Writing the line as /.claude/* ignores the same files and lets the negation work. The description's Testing section then expects .gitignore:2:/.claude/* from git check-ignore -v.
